locations.label: Locations
locations.description: Points of interest by category and location, on a map.

useCase.headline: Where the estate sits: every location on a map, counted and split by category, as the starting point for a new domain.
useCase.businessQuestion: Where are our locations, and how do they break down by category and type?
talkTrack: Read the header: total locations, distinct categories and distinct location types.
Show the category breakdown and name the dominant category.
Put the locations on the map and pan to the area that matters to the customer.
Say what this view becomes once retargeted: the estate, depot or site view for the customer's own domain.
snowflakeCapabilities: Locations stored as native GEOGRAPHY and rendered to the map straight from SQL
A config-driven view: this page is JSON over the neutral contract, with no application code
One query path feeding the dashboard and the Cortex agent alike
dataRequired: A location master with a name, a category or type, and a point location
valueDrivers: A working view on day one of a retargeting, before any custom build
One shared picture of the estate instead of a spreadsheet per team
useCase.method: Counts come from the starter pack's VW_LOCATIONS contract view, and the map plots each location's GEOGRAPHY point directly. Category and type are whatever the source data supplies - nothing is derived.
useCase.caveats: This is a starter-pack placeholder over STARTER_APP.CORE, not a finished use case. Rewrite every field here when you retarget the app: the headline, business question, audience and industries all surface in the per-view info overlay AND in the chat agent's solution catalog, so leaving this text in place tells a customer they are looking at a scaffold.

data.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS locations, COUNT(DISTINCT CATEGORY) AS categories, COUNT(DISTINCT LOCATION_TYPE) AS types FROM STARTER_APP.CORE.VW_LOCATIONS
SELECT CATEGORY AS category, COUNT(*) AS locations FROM STARTER_APP.CORE.VW_LOCATIONS GROUP BY CATEGORY ORDER BY locations DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT NAME AS name, CATEGORY AS category, LNG AS lng, LAT AS lat FROM STARTER_APP.CORE.VW_LOCATIONS WHERE LAT IS NOT NULL AND LNG IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5000

movements.label: Movements
movements.description: Origin-to-destination movements: volume, distance, duration, and daily trend.

useCase.headline: Origin-to-destination movement: how much moves, how far, how long it takes, and how that trends by day.
useCase.businessQuestion: What is moving between our locations, and is the volume or the distance changing?
talkTrack: Read the header: movement count, average distance, average duration and total distance.
Show the daily trend and say whether volume or distance is rising.
Use the daily table to pick out an outlier day, then ask the customer what happened that day.
Say what this becomes after retargeting: the shipment, journey or job-flow view for their domain.
snowflakeCapabilities: Movement facts and a pre-aggregated daily rollup served from the same contract, with no cube to maintain
A config-driven view: JSON over the neutral contract, with no application code
One query path behind the KPIs, the chart, the table and the agent's answer
dataRequired: Movement records with an origin, a destination, a timestamp, and distance or duration
Optional: a daily rollup, if raw volume makes per-day aggregation expensive
valueDrivers: See flow and its trend without building a reporting layer first
Establish the baseline that later optimization work is measured against
useCase.method: The KPIs aggregate the starter pack's VW_MOVEMENTS contract view; the trend chart and the daily table read the VW_MOVEMENT_DAILY rollup. Distance and duration are taken from the source records rather than recomputed from geometry.
useCase.caveats: Starter-pack placeholder over STARTER_APP.CORE, not a finished use case. Rewrite every field when retargeting - this text surfaces in the per-view info overlay AND in the chat agent's solution catalog. Distance and duration are whatever the source supplies, so do not present them as road-network measurements unless the source made them so.

data.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS movements, ROUND(AVG(DISTANCE_KM),2) AS avg_km, ROUND(AVG(DURATION_MINUTES),1) AS avg_min, ROUND(SUM(DISTANCE_KM),0) AS total_km FROM STARTER_APP.CORE.VW_MOVEMENTS
SELECT TO_VARCHAR(DAY) AS day, MOVEMENT_COUNT AS movements, TOTAL_DISTANCE_KM AS total_km FROM STARTER_APP.CORE.VW_MOVEMENT_DAILY ORDER BY DAY ASC

SELECT TO_VARCHAR(DAY) AS day, MOVEMENT_COUNT AS movements, AVG_DISTANCE_KM AS avg_km, AVG_DURATION_MINUTES AS avg_min, TOTAL_DISTANCE_KM AS total_km FROM STARTER_APP.CORE.VW_MOVEMENT_DAILY ORDER BY DAY ASC
